In New York City, composting is also supposed to save money by reducing the amount of trash the city hauls to landfills, many of which are out of state.
But the program hasn't gone exactly as planned.
The city's brown bin composting initiative started as a pilot program 13 years ago under Mayor Michael Bloomberg.
Mayor Bill de Blasio wanted to expand the program, but the expansion was put on hold due to exploding costs and low participation rates.
The city was spending an estimated six times as much to collect compost as regular trash.
Those high costs came from operating special composting trucks that were carrying relatively little waste.
